lines.text: When electricity enters your body, it looks for the fastest path to ground.
That path runs straight through your heart.
Just sixty milliamps — the power of a small light bulb — is enough to kill you.
The current hijacks your nervous system and locks every muscle in your body.
You cannot let go of the wire.
Your heart begins fibrillating — quivering instead of pumping.
Internally, the current has scorched a path through your organs.
Lightning does the opposite — the bolt is so brief your heart stops then restarts.
That is why lightning strike survivors can walk away.
But a household socket holds on long enough to end you.
